MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 14, 2026
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on April 14, 2026, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 9, 2026, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ruesch
  Council Member Vasquez (arrived 5:01pm)
  Mayor Bucknum
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  Tarquin Preziosi, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation. Paragraph (1) of subdivision
  (d) of Government Code Section 54956.9: Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v. Mission
  Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-01376969-CU-MC-CJC

 CS2.  Conference with Real Property Negotiators. Government Code Section 54956.8.
  Property Los Osos, 25282 Marguerite Parkway: Agency Negotiators; Elaine Lister,
  City Manager, Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager, and Tarquin Preziosi, City
  Attorney: Negotiating Party: Santa Margarita Water District General Manager:
  Under Negotiation: Price and Terms

City Council Minutes  1  April 14, 2026
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 pm Mayor Bucknum recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:00 pm Mayor
Bucknum reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

 City Attorney Perziosi announced that there were two properly agendized items with no reportable
 action.

 INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ruesch

 PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Recognize the Mission Viejo Elks Lodge

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamation to Alan Harkness, Exalted Ruler Elect.

 P2.  Recognize Love Mission Viejo

  Mayor Bucknum presented proclamation to Sharon Genton.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Grant Chambers, M.V.: Provided the City Council with pictures and photographs of the American
  flag in Sheboygan, Wisconsin, which stands on a 400-foot flagpole. He proposed that Mission Viejo
  explore opportunities to surpass that height and claim the title of having the tallest flagpole in North
  America.

  Charles Manazir, M.V.: Requested that the City Council formally recognize two distinguished
  longtime residents - astronaut Mike Lopez Alagria, Class of 1976, and his son, Admiral Michael
  Minazer, Class of 1977. Given their unique achievements, he respectfully recommended that the
  Council consider some form of recognition for them.

  Everest Saine, M.V.: Spoke on the Community Character Trait of the Month Service. He
  highlighted its importance and gave examples of the trait Service.

  Debra Lewandowski, M.V.: Critiqued the City’s approval of Vista del Lago Apartment Expansion
  citing insufficient community outreach and inconsistent project scrutiny. Requested details on
  developer negotiations and proposed implementing resident-only parking permits for the Pinecrest
  area.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Referenced the recent Planning and Transportation Commission review of
  existing and proposed surface parking plans at the Marguerite Tennis and Aquatics Center. He
City Council Minutes  2  April 14, 2026
   requested that the Assistant City Manager develop a long-term parking structure plan and urged
  consideration of a multi-story parking structure to preserve green space and accommodate future
  growth, rather than temporary surface lot expansions.

  Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Provided the City Council with a recent image of the President. He addressed
  recent controversial actions by the President and questioned the Council’s political affiliations and
  religious beliefs. Lastly, he acknowledged that the city is functioning well and urged the Council to
  work toward creating a better future for the next generation.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item 13 was removed from the Consent Calendar for a separate discussion.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Ruesch, to approve the
  Consent Calendar outlined below.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of March 24, 2026, as
  presented.

 2.  General Check Register Dated March 13, 2026, in the Amount of $3,305,511.57

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 3.  General Check Register Dated March 20, 2026, in the Amount of $1,328,037.80

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  General Check Register dated March 27, 2026, in the amount of $1,213,859.15

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 5.  Golf Check Register Dated March 13, 2026, in the Amount of $13,305.56

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 6.  Golf Check Register Dated March 20, 2026, in the Amount of $124,755.30

  Ratified the accompanying check register.
City Council Minutes  3  April 14, 2026
  7.  Golf Check Register Dated March 27, 2026, in the Amount of $17,700.47

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 8.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for February 2026

  Received and filed.

 9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for February 2026

  Received and filed.

 10.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for
  February 2026

  Received and filed.

 11.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly
  Report for February 2026

  Received and filed.

 12.  Adding Chapter 11.26 (Prohibition on the Sale and Distribution of Kratom Products)
  to Title 11 of the Mission Viejo City Code

  Adopted Ordinance 26-361 Adding Chapter 11.26 (Prohibition on the Sale and
  Distribution of Kratom Products) to Title 11 of the Mission Viejo City Code.

 14.  Draft Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Annual Action Plan for the Expenditure of Fiscal Year
  2026-2027 CDBG Funds

  Adopted Resolution 26-13 Approving the City’s Draft Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Annual
  Action Plan for the Expenditure of Fiscal Year 2026-2027 CDBG Funds, and Authorizing
  Submission of the Plan to the United States Department of Housing and Urban
  Development.

 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 13.  Budget Amendment For the North Oso Creek Bike/Pedestrian Trail Open Space
  Project CIP 22333

City Council Minutes  4  April 14, 2026
   Assistant City Manager Hill presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 26-12 Amending the North Oso Creek Bike/Pedestrian Trail Open Space
  Project CIP 22333 and Adjustments in Certain Funds

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 NEW BUSINESS

 15.  Cooperation Agreement (CDBG Funds Transfer for Affordable Housing) between the
  City of Mission Viejo and Mission Viejo Housing Authority; and Affordable Housing
  and CDBG Loan Agreement between the Mission Viejo Housing Authority and
  WISEPlace, a California Nonprofit, Public Benefit Corporation.

  Planning and Economic Development Manager Cliff Jones presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to (1) Adopt
  Joint Resolution 26-14 of the City Council and MVHA Approving the Cooperation
  Agreement A26-13 (CDBG Funds Transfer for Affordable Housing) for Transfer of $530,000
  of CDBG Funds to Implement the Affordable Housing and CDBG Loan Agreement and
  Making Certain Other Findings; and (2) adopt MVHA Resolution 26-01 Approving the
  Affordable Housing and CDBG Loan Agreement between the MVHA and WISEPlace to
  Provide a CDBG Loan for Acquisition and Long-Term Operation of Two Condominium
  Homes for Tenancy and Occupancy by Qualified Very Low Income Households Who are at
  Risk of Homelessness or Homeless, and Making Certain Other Findings; (3) adopt City
  Council Resolution 26-15 Approving CDBG Fund Budget Transfer to Housing Authority
  Fund; and (4) adopt MVHA Resolution 26-02 Approving Receipt and Use of CDBG funds
  for Affordable Housing Loan.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 16.  Property Access Agreement between the Mission Viejo Housing Authority/City of
  Mission Viejo and Trumark Homes for Due Diligence Work Related to Potential
  Purchase and Development of the Surplus Property Owned by the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority and the City of Mission Viejo and Identified as Housing Site 3 of
  the City of Mission Viejo 2021-2029 Housing Element

City Council Minutes  5  April 14, 2026
   Director of Community Development Larry Longenecker presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  approve the Property Access Agreement A26-14 with Trumark Homes for Site 3 and
  Authorized the City Manager to Execute the Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 CITY MANAGER REPORTS

 City Manager Lister proudly announced that the Mission Viejo Animal Services team was honored
 as the 2026 Agency of the Year by the National Animal Care and Control Association, recognizing
 their outstanding dedication and impact in animal care. She also shared that goats have returned to
 the open space between Jeronimo and Casa Del Sol for vegetation management and are expected to
 remain there for two to three weeks. Additionally, mini goats will be featured at the upcoming Arbor
 Day event for meet and greet activities. Lastly, City Manager Lister reported that a 10-week-old
 female puppy, recently abandoned overnight at the Animal Services facility, is doing well and
 receiving loving care from staff.

 CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

 City Attorney Preziosi provided an update on the legal action by Southern California Edison against
 the State Board of Equalization, which seeks to reduce property taxes for the past five years due to
 California wildfires. New estimates from HDL indicate that if the action succeeds, Mission Viejo
 could face a financial impact of approximately $206,000.

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

 Council Member Kelley

 Council Member Kelley shared that she serves on a policy committee for the League of California
 Cities and recently attended a meeting where she gained valuable information. She praised the City’s
 Marine Adoption Committee, acknowledging the efforts of members and volunteers in hosting a
 successful “Day in Paradise” event for the Marines and their families. She also expressed gratitude
City Council Minutes  6  April 14, 2026
  to the Orange County Sheriff’s Department for their support during the event. Councilmember
 Kelley attended the “Meet the Mayors” event on April 2, which featured Mayor Bucknum and
 mayors from South Orange County. Additionally, she highlighted the success of the Master
 Gardener Expo and Plant Giveaway held on April 11, which drew around 2,000 attendees. She
 commended staff members Melanie McGrane and Mike Swingholm for their dedication. Lastly, she
 joined Council Member Ruesch at the Vocational Visions Gala, highlighting the valued partnership
 the organization has with Mission Viejo.

 Council Member Ruesch

 Council Member Ruesch recapped hosting visitors from Wako, Japan, who toured the city's lake
 and amenities as part of early discussions about a potential sister city relationship. He also described
 working with Slovakian representatives exploring various sports facilities in Mission Viejo for
 Olympic training. He showed a short video sharing his experience participating in a physically
 demanding fireman’s competition organized by Firefighters Local 3631 and OCFA, which included
 tasks like repelling from buildings and venting roofs, ending with a race up a six-story tower. He
 suggested considering an event or recognition for Armed Forces recruitment during the city’s 250th
 anniversary. Finally, he proposed adding an agenda item to explore offering lifetime family
 memberships to recreation facilities for past Council Members, aiming to support their health and
 maintain their involvement as valuable community ambassadors. He requested staff research
 participation and costs for this proposal to be presented in May.

 Council Member Vasquez

 Council Member Vasquez stated she attended several community events, including Springtime in
 Paris Boutique, a Senior Grocery Easter meal distribution, the UC Master Gardeners Expo, where
 attendees could get gardening advice, and an OC Forum event focused on women's empowerment
 and financial leadership. Additionally, she is preparing to take her Girl Scout Troop camping soon
 and shared that her youngest child enjoyed an affordable spring break camp at the Montanoso
 Recreation Center.

 Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

 Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that the Sports and Economic Tourism Committee will be
 meeting tomorrow to discuss various topics. He highlighted recent visits from representatives of
 Slovakia and the Netherlands, as they consider Mission Viejo as a training base for the 2028
 Olympics. He also noted that the city will be hosting a Paralympic swimming camp this summer at
 the Marguerite Aquatics Center. Additionally, Mayor Pro Tem Goodell shared that the Nadadores is
 pursuing a bid to host the United States Olympic Team Diving Trials, and discussions are underway
 to establish a local USA Diving office in Mission Viejo due to the increased activity. Overall, he
 expressed enthusiasm about the city’s expanding role in sports and tourism.

City Council Minutes  7  April 14, 2026
  Mayor Bucknum

 Mayor Bucknum was honored to present a 100th birthday certificate to Evelyn Ritterswerden, a
 longtime resident of Mission Viejo. She shared that she now serves on the Nadadores Board of
 Directors and recently attended a meeting. Mayor Bucknum also participated in various community
 events, including the Springtime in Paris Boutique, the Mission Viejo High School versus Trabuco
 Hills High School golf match, the Meet the Mayors event, and a Sensory-friendly Concert with the
 Pacific Symphony. Additionally, she met with the Mayor of Wako, Japan, to explore a potential
 sister city relationship. She highlighted upcoming community events such as a presentation by three
 Holocaust survivors on April 22, Earth Day/Arbor Day on April 25, the Orange County Triathlon
 on April 26 with related street closures, the Library's Purse Palooza fundraiser on May 2, and the
 Mission Viejo Rotary Mayor's Prayer Breakfast on May 6 featuring guest speaker Rod Karu.

 ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 7:42 pm, with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
 Bucknum adjourned the to Tuesday, April 28, 2026, at 5:00 p.m.

 Renata Winter
 Assistant City Clerk

City Council Minutes  8  April 14, 2026
